children.value: Offing analyzes software repositories on the user's computer. The Codex and Claude plugins start a local stdio MCP server and do not send repository contents to an Offing-operated service. Offing does not require an Offing account, collect analytics, use advertising identifiers, or sell personal data.

The local tools read supported manifests, lockfiles, workflow files, runtime-version files, and relevant source excerpts from the repository path the user authorizes. Results can contain file paths and short source excerpts. The host application receives those results, so its privacy policy and the user's workspace settings also apply.
The plugin launches the exact published

npm version recorded in its manifest. The package manager may contact the configured npm registry to obtain that package. Lifecycle evidence links are returned as references; Offing does not open them automatically.
Scans use no network. The one exception is

, which you run yourself to fetch newer lifecycle rules between releases. Rules ship inside each release; that command downloads a public release list and two public files (the signed bundle and its signature) from the project's GitHub releases, verifies the Sigstore signature offline against a trusted root that ships in the package, and activates the new rules only after verification succeeds. If verification fails, Offing keeps the rules bundled with the installed release and reports why. Pinning with
